The GeoTIFF coverage is a two-dimensional numeric array, so NoData is numeric.
ArcGIS Pro's Make WCS Layer tool is available in Basic, Standard and Advanced licences.
The ArcGIS guidance says to enter the WCS endpoint only through the question mark.
The OS Terrain source DTM is captured as a triangulated irregular network.
The TIN is edited using mass points and breaklines and may also use automated methods.
Source capture is performed in a photogrammetric environment.
TIN triangles retain feature edges more accurately than a regular grid.
Both grid and contour products are interpolated from the source TIN.
The TIN is not widely supported by GIS software.
OS Terrain 50 uses a more generalised representation for small-scale use.
Minimum product coverage extends to the low-water mark.
For England and Wales the low-water limit is Mean Low Water.
For Scotland the low-water limit is Mean Low Water Springs.
Land represented within inland water bodies must at least have its outer edge captured.
Surrounding inland water is modelled as flat.
Other land in inland water captured only by automated processes is removed.
Height accuracy is organised into urban/major routes, rural, and mountain/moorland classes.
Source z values must meet RMSE requirements appropriate to their geographic class.
Source surface X and Y coordinates are eastings and northings in OSGB36.
Source Z coordinates are heights in metres relative to the applicable datum.
Most areas use Ordnance Survey Newlyn Datum.
A small number of offshore islands use a local vertical datum.
The bare-earth surface excludes buildings, supported structures and vegetation.
Ground obstructions such as dams, breakwaters, wide groynes and earthworks can be part of bare earth.
Only terrain features expected to persist through at least the next revision period are modelled.
Underground features are not recorded in the DTM.
Overhead features are removed from the DTM.
The DTM is intended to be free from spikes and wells that do not reflect terrain.
Road carriageways and railway track beds are modelled as smooth surfaces.
Most data should display without visible tile edges or discernible height differences.
Small tile edges can occur in tidal areas because of local tidal differences.
Supported structures include bridges, viaducts, cranes, elevated buildings and leg-supported piers.
Supported structures are removed where an air gap separates them from bare earth.
Hedgerows and trees are removed to represent bare earth.
The top of a vertical feature is recorded at its correct planimetric location.
The lowest point can be planimetrically offset so one location has only one z value.
Major road and rail limits, slopes and embankments are modelled to reflect real-world shape.
The outer limits, shape and depth of mineral workings and landfill sites are captured.
Temporary spoil heaps that do not represent the terrain are removed.
Flat-water bodies larger than 0.7 hectares have their limits captured.
The documentation equates the threshold with more than 7000 cubic metres capacity.
The recorded water height is the lowest height of surrounding data.
The modelled water surface is flat.
OS Terrain 50 contours are supplied as a single national GeoPackage file.
The GeoPackage contains spot_height, land_water_boundary and contour_line layers.
OS Terrain 50 online download is available without registration.
